item.title: Dave Chappelle Pops Up In The Most Unlikely Place
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: An AllHipHop source says Dave Chappelle and musician Frédéric Yonnet dropped in on Howard University’s tribute to Stevie Wonder and watched the students run the show.
item.content:encoded:
Dave Chappelle slipped into Howard University’s tribute to Stevie Wonder on Tuesday, according to an AllHipHop source, but left the show to the students.

Now, I may have oversold the “unlikely” part. If you saw Dave at Capital One Arena on Monday night, you already know he was in Washington, D.C. And he was in a Stevie Wonder kind of mood. The concert setlist puts him onstage for “Superstition.”

A night later, according to my “source,” all he needed was a seat.

Howard U was celebrating 50 years of Songs in the Key of Life, the 1976 album that gave us “Sir Duke,” “I Wish” and “As.” You know, the music AI can’t bless us with. Stevie, 76, had just played an arena and still made time to speak with students the next day. I get tired when somebody asks me to make two stops on the way home. Or typing this article.

My source says there was a little commotion when Dave arrived with musician Frédéric Yonnet and a few others. The hosts acknowledged the group, everybody took their seats and the program carried on. Students did most of the hosting, and Dave and company stayed for the show before taking off. My source also says camera use was restricted inside. So if you’re waiting for a grainy photo, I’ve got nothing for you.

Stevie, meanwhile, moves presidential. From what I hear, Howard kept security tight around him amid all that fanfare. Obama would be proud. Between an arena show on Monday and a campus tribute on Tuesday, I can see why the university would want to keep things orderly. Everybody wants a minute with Stevie. Do the math on that in a room full of people who grew up on his records.

So did Dave come back for another dose of Stevie, or did he want to see what Howard’s students had put together? Could’ve been both. I haven’t heard his reason. What I like about the whole thing is that the students got to run a show with Stevie Wonder in the room and Dave Chappelle in the audience. Imagine trying to concentrate with that kind of pressure.

item.title: YNW Melly Gets More Time To Exchange Evidence Before Murder Retrial
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: A Broward judge gives YNW Melly more time for pretrial filings and evidence exchange before a December 17 hearing.
item.content:encoded:
YNW Melly‘s lawyers have until December 11 to exchange evidence and file pretrial requests ahead of his double-murder retrial. Broward Circuit Judge Martin Fein granted the defense more time on Monday, November 23, according to New documents reviewed by AllHipHop.com.

The new deadline falls six days before Melly’s next hearing. The clerk recorded an order allowing him to wear civilian clothes and shoes in court on December 17.

While the defense gained more time to file, two of its existing requests over what jurors can hear stayed alive.

Fein rejected prosecutors’ efforts to dismiss them: one asking him to keep Melly’s lyrics and videos out of the retrial and another asking him to exclude alleged gang evidence and related expert testimony.

The added time gives prosecutors a chance to question four defense experts before Fein decides whether any can testify at trial.

In courtroom footage posted by journalist Meghann Cuniff, Fein said the defense had disclosed the experts late but deferred a decision on excluding them so the state could take their depositions.

Two witnesses would address rap lyrics, while the other two would respond to the state’s evidence from a forensic pathologist and a bloodstain analyst.

Fein said the chance to question those witnesses depends on whether they make themselves available. “If these people don’t make themselves available for the depositions, and it’s going to be a pretty tight time frame, I probably will strike them,” he said.

Fein’s decision on the filing deadline didn’t settle the dispute over what evidence jurors can hear.

During the same hearing, defense lawyer Drew Findling pointed to how little prosecutors discussed gangs in their closing argument at the first trial.

Fein deferred a ruling on whether prosecutors can introduce gang evidence at the retrial.

The evidence disputes come ahead of a second trial on charges that Melly killed fellow rappers YNW Juvy and YNW Sakchaser in October 2018.

He pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder, and the first trial ended in July 2023 after jurors couldn’t agree on a verdict.

Jury selection for the retrial remains on the calendar for January 6, 2027.

item.title: Meek Mill Wants Out Of Live Nation Deal As Five Tour Dates Are Canceled
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Meek Mill asks to get out of his Live Nation agreement as the five remaining dates on his Dream Chasers Nights run are canceled.
item.content:encoded:
Meek Mill wants out of his Live Nation deal and all five remaining stops on his Dream Chasers Nights tour are off.

Ticketmaster lists the shows as canceled just days after the Philadelphia rapper opened the run in his hometown.

Meek made his request public in a post on X late Wednesday.

“I feel trapped and shelved behind this contract I tried to reach out to everybody they played me like im not aware!” Meek wrote.

Meek described the deal as exclusive in a follow-up post and said the dates he had been offered weren’t ones he was comfortable with.

He also questioned whether he’d play New York, although the city wasn’t on the announced six-stop itinerary. Live Nation hasn’t publicly confirmed that the agreement Meek described has ended or explained why the shows were canceled.

Live Nation Urban partnered with Meek on the run announced in October, starting with the November 24 homecoming at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

That show went ahead, and Meek acknowledged Live Nation’s role in it even as he criticized the arrangement.

The itinerary called for him to play Hollywood Palladium on November 29, MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston on December 5 and CFG Bank Arena in Baltimore on December 11, before heading to Chicago’s Aragon Ballroom on December 18 and Atlanta’s Coca-Cola Roxy on December 20.

Ticketmaster’s Hollywood cancellation notice says the event organizer called off the show, but it doesn’t give a reason.

People who bought tickets directly won’t need to request a refund, according to the notice.

The vendor says it will send the money back to the original payment method once it receives the funds from the organizer, and refunds on transferred tickets go to the original buyer.

Meek told followers he intended to reschedule the canceled shows and put his own money into a promotion business under the Dream Chasers name.

He didn’t provide replacement dates in those posts, and Ticketmaster’s listing didn’t show new dates for any of the five cities.

Meek also said he was willing to step down after naming REFORM in an earlier post.

“Next reform meeting I gotta pull out too becaus I’m trapped in a contacts with somebody on the board and everybody know but nobody speaking up … I can’t do charity like that! I gotta go with another foundation with great meaning because even that went beyond me and my agenda,”Meek fumed.

He co-chairs REFORM Alliance with Michael Rubin and Jay-Z; Live Nation CEO Michael Rapino sits on its board. Meek didn’t name the board member he meant or announce a resignation.

item.title: Joy Reid Reignites Nicki Minaj Feud With Sarah Baartman Comparison
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Joy Reid questions what Nicki Minaj gains from backing Trump and draws a distinction between the rapper and Sarah Baartman.
item.content:encoded:
Joy Reid reopened her feud with Nicki Minaj by comparing the way Donald Trump’s movement presents the rapper to the public display of Sarah Baartman. The former MSNBC host made the comparison in an interview on Club Shay Shay after Shannon Sharpe asked if she’d gone too far by calling Minaj a MAGA “house pet.”

Reid conceded the old phrase might have been harsh but stood by her criticism. “Nicki Minaj is putting herself on display for MAGA in a way that’s undignified for her, that is questionable as to the motivation. And one wonders like what do they have on her or what does she need that she feels like she needs to do this?” Reid said.

Reid drew a distinction between Minaj’s decision to support the movement and what happened to Baartman. Baartman was a South African woman exhibited in Europe in the early 19th century, and Reid stressed that she hadn’t chosen to be put on display. Reid argued that Minaj, by contrast, had chosen to appear alongside Trump and that the way he presented her was dehumanizing.

Reid said she doubted the people celebrating Minaj’s politics knew her music.

The two first clashed publicly in September 2021 after Minaj shared an unsubstantiated claim about the COVID-19 vaccine. Reid told viewers on MSNBC’s The ReidOut that Minaj was using her reach to discourage people from protecting themselves, and said she was disappointed as a fan.

Minaj fired back that Reid “didn’t bother to read all my tweets” and accused the host of misrepresenting her on TV. She pointed to other posts where she’d said she would probably get vaccinated before touring.

Reid shifted the dispute to Trump’s politics in February on Don Lemon’s show, saying Republicans wanted Minaj for Black “cultural cool” rather than for her music. Minaj went back to the vaccine dispute on July 31, mocking Reid in a post written as a fake diary entry from Anthony Fauci as Trump adviser Alex Bruesewitz called for critics to apologize.

Minaj has defended her support for Trump in her own interviews, telling Lara Trump that she loves the president and doesn’t make excuses for it.

item.title: Lil Baby’s Old Atlanta Hangout Makes Way For $450 Million Redevelopment
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Baby's old hangout and back-to-school giveaway site gives way to a $450 million housing and retail project in Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby used to bring Atlanta families to the Mall West End for his back-to-school festival.

Now crews are taking apart the shopping center that doubled as a neighborhood gathering place, clearing the way for a $450 million redevelopment in southwest Atlanta.

The demolition began this week at the corner of Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard and Lee Street, according to WSB-TV.

Casey Dantzler went there Wednesday, November 25, and left carrying two bricks he wanted to keep as a piece of Atlanta history.

“I’ve been going to this mall since I was probably 7 years old,” Dantzler told the station.

The mall was a regular stop for Lil Baby long before he used it to host his 2022 Back to School Fest.

He ordered lemon-pepper wings from its American Deli so often that he started calling one of the workers Mama.

He partnered with Goodr for a giveaway that offered backpacks, sneakers, haircuts and carnival rides to more than 3,000 children from southwest Atlanta.

Lil Baby also invested in an earlier plan to redevelop the property, but that proposal wasn’t the one Atlanta ultimately took up. The city announced the site’s acquisition in October 2024 through Atlanta Urban Development and Atlanta Beltline, naming BRP Companies and The Prusik Group as the developers.

The current plan, called One West End, replaces the enclosed mall with housing for people at different incomes, outdoor gathering space and new storefronts.

The shopping center closed at the end of January 2025, but the developers offered tenants who wanted to stay temporary space on the property.

The project’s website lists American Deli among those businesses, alongside Dendera Cosmetics, The Burning Sands and Planet Fitness.

One West End will build on more than five decades of Black-owned commerce at the site.

The new project sets aside about 120,000 square feet for stores and services, with plans for a grocery store.

One West End’s developers also plan to add more than 300 student beds in coordination with the nearby Atlanta University Center.

item.title: Cardi B Turns Her Year Of Touring And Motherhood Into A Pep Talk
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B looks back on an arena tour, a new baby and launching Grow-Good, then asks other women what they could do in a year.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B asked other women to think about what they could do with a year after she spent hers juggling tour rehearsals and four kids.

In a post on X, the Bronx rapper looked back on releasing an album, having a baby, taking on endorsement deals and starting a hair care company.

“In one year I dropped a album.. had a baby… then went straight into rehearsals for a whole month away from my kids… spent three months on tour… stacked endorsements… and launched a super successful hair business all while mothering four babies. I did all of that in one year!!!” Cardi B said proudly.

The stretch she described included a month of rehearsals away from her children before she hit the road.

“So imagine what you could do in one year sister!! Get up and go get it!” Cardi B wrote.

The album that sent her out on the road was Am I the Drama?, her second studio release, which Atlantic Records put out on September 19, 2025. Cardi B announced the birth of her fourth child that November, and the Little Miss Drama Tour opened on February 11 at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, California.

Cardi B was still on that first headlining arena tour when her hair care line Grow-Good Beauty went on sale April 15.

The debut included six products, and the run ended three days later with her second night at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena.

She told NBC’s Today during the run that she’d been balancing the shows with raising her children and planned to keep releasing music once the tour was over.

Grow-Good started shipping to Canada by the time Cardi returned to Toronto for Billboard Canada’s Women in Music ceremony on November 24.

She accepted its first Global Woman of the Year award at Rebel and thanked Summer Walker from the stage for supporting her away from the cameras.

Cardi B also used her post to call herself Canada’s most certified female rapper.

Music Canada’s public database lists individual certifications rather than a ranking of female rappers, and Cardi didn’t specify whether she meant the number of certified releases or their combined certification levels. Billboard Canada’s announcement used a different measure: It credited her with 46 entries on the Canadian Hot 100, eight of them in the top 10.

One of those records is “WAP,” her collaboration with Megan Thee Stallion, which Music Canada certified nine times platinum on February 17.

item.title: King Von’s “Took Her To The O” Reaches 1 Billion Spotify Streams
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: King Von's 2020 Chicago drill single "Took Her To The O" is his first track to reach 1 billion Spotify streams, per ChartMasters.
item.content:encoded:
King Von‘s “Took Her To The O” has passed 1 billion streams on Spotify.

The Chicago rapper’s 2020 single became the first track in his catalog to reach the mark, according to independent streaming tracker ChartMasters.

ChartMasters listed the song at 1,000,350,837 plays in its November 21 update.

A November 20 snapshot from Kworb had it just under the line, at 999,424,947.

The single came out February 21, 2020, before appearing on Von’s LeVon James project that March. Chopsquad DJ produced the piano-led track, which followed the scene-by-scene style Von had used on his breakout, “Crazy Story.”

In the official video, director Joan Pabon cut between the story and a therapy session where Von narrates it.

Von thought the novels he’d read while incarcerated might have shaped how he told stories. “I like to read, and there were a lot of books when I was locked up,” he told Passion of the Weiss in an interview.

The song had already pulled in more than 12 million total streams by the time LeVon James arrived, according to the project’s original press release.

That figure covered the song’s early run across services rather than Spotify alone. The project came out through Lil Durk’s Only The Family and EMPIRE.

G Herbo guested on “On Yo Ass” while Von was opening for him on the PTSD tour, and Lil Durk appeared on two of the project’s songs.

The cover also played on the title, with Von recreating LeBron James’ pregame chalk toss.

AllHipHop reported that the single was one of four Von tracks on the Billboard Hot 100 shortly after his November 2020 death.

It debuted at No. 47, above “The Code” with Polo G and “All These Niggas” with Lil Durk. The song drew 11.9 million U.S. streams in the week ending November 12, a 258% jump according to MRC Data’s year-end report.

In the same Spotify ranking, ChartMasters puts “Crazy Story, Pt. 3” second at roughly 543 million plays and the original “Crazy Story” third at roughly 495 million.

item.title: Rod Wave Asked Judge To Let Him Finish His Tour Before Battery Trial
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Rod Wave asked for time to finish his 33-show tour, and a judge granted the request, moving his battery trial to December 14.
item.content:encoded:
Rod Wave asked a judge to let him finish his arena tour before he was due to stand trial on a misdemeanor battery charge. The judge granted his request and moved the trial from October 26 to December 14, according to court records obtained by TMZ.

Rod Wave cited the scale of the 33-show run across 25 cities in making his case for the delay. His filing described a tour that “employs more than 100 people and sold approximately 500,000 tickets to his fans,” according to TMZ. He also told the court that the production cost $3 million.

That stretch on the road came as Rod Wave was rolling out Don’t Look Down, the album that shares its name with the tour. The arena run began in Philadelphia in September with two nights at Xfinity Mobile Arena, and Mainstay Touring produced it. Fridayy joined him as a special guest on the run, which was billed as Rod Wave’s biggest headlining tour when it was announced.

The trial concerns a 2020 incident in which Rod Wave is accused of scratching a man’s knees. TMZ identified the man as Pierre Lamartiniere and reported that the rapper was arrested in 2021 and released on bond. The court ordered him not to contact Lamartiniere.

The battery case had already gone through a diversion program before the new trial date came into play. TMZ reported that the program required Rod Wave to complete anger management and make an anti-violence video for Atlanta Public Schools. Prosecutors asked to revoke his probation after he was arrested again in 2025.

The 2025 arrests are the basis for two separate cases, not the battery charge behind the December trial. One stems from an April 2025 incident at his home in Milton, Georgia, and includes an aggravated assault allegation involving a firearm. The other arose from a November 2025 traffic stop in Atlanta and led to a recent indictment on drug and gun charges that also includes a reckless driving count.

Rod Wave has denied the allegations of wrongdoing, and his lawyers have separately challenged the circumstances of the Atlanta traffic stop.

item.title: Coachella Sues Walmart Over Merchandise Sold Under Festival’s Name
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Coachella takes Walmart to court over apparel, drinkware and displays the festival says used its branding without a license.
item.content:encoded:
Coachella took Walmart to federal court over festival-branded goods that it says showed up in stores near the concert grounds and on Walmart’s website.

Coachella Music Festival and promoter Goldenvoice filed the complaint November 24 in the Central District of California, naming both Walmart Inc. and Wal-Mart.com USA, LLC as defendants.

The most recent store examples in the filing come from April 2026, when the organizers say Walmart’s La Quinta location offered apparel bearing Coachella’s branding.

They allege the store displayed a Ferris wheel sign made by festival sponsor Absolut Vodka near the merchandise. The filing also points to videos showing bottles, tumblers, tank tops and other items at Walmart’s North Indio store.

The organizers trace their dispute with the retailer back to a set of online listings in June 2017.

They allege Walmart advertised at least 28 items of clothing under the Coachella name and say the retailer eventually removed them and shared contact information for the outside manufacturers.

The suit accuses Walmart of selling goods itself and letting others sell and advertise them through its stores and website.

The first in-store sales described in the suit came two years after those online listings, at the North Indio location. The organizers say Walmart removed that clothing after a demand, and later took down ads at La Quinta that drew from Coachella lineup posters to sell folding chairs and coolers. “Plaintiffs’ requests have been of minimal benefit; Walmart typically stops for a period of time, but then resumes its infringing conduct,” the organizers allege.

Coachella runs its own merchandise tent and online shop, and organizers say unauthorized products could leave shoppers thinking the festival approved them.

The suit points to the festival name, its palm-tree logo and its overall look, including the Ferris wheel, as the festival prepares for its 2027 edition. The Associated Press footage below shows the wheel at the 2026 festival.

The plaintiffs want the court to block Walmart from using the marks in sales or ads, including through third-party vendors.

They’re seeking Walmart’s profits from the alleged infringement and asking the court to triple damages on the claim that the violations were deliberate.

The complaint doesn’t specify a dollar amount.

Coachella Music Festival and Goldenvoice have asked for a jury trial on the claims.

item.title: U-God Breaks Eight-Year Solo Hiatus With “Rock So Many” Ahead Of Wu-Tang Halftime
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: U-God puts Wu-Tang's touring history on screen as he brings out the first track from his next solo album, Stinger.
item.content:encoded:
U-God turned years of Wu-Tang Clan tour footage into the first look at his next solo album. The rapper released “Rock So Many” on Wednesday, his first solo single and video in eight years, according to his representative. DJ Homicide produced the track, which leads into Stinger, U-God’s sixth solo studio album, due in early 2027.

The video pulls together hundreds of photos and clips from Wu-Tang shows around the world. U-God’s representative said he made it to thank the photographers who documented those nights. The rapper took stock of his time onstage with the group as he announced the release: “I can’t believe we ROCK SO MANY.”

The new album will follow Venom, the solo project U-God released through Babygrande Records in March 2018. That record arrived in the same month as his memoir Raw: My Journey Into the Wu-Tang, which told the group’s story from his point of view. DJ Homicide worked with U-God on the 2018 mixtape Bring Back God II, reworking tracks including “Keynote Speaker” and “Zilla.”

U-God’s recording career outside the group goes back to Golden Arms Redemption, his 1999 solo debut. That album included the track “Rumble,” which was used in the group’s video game Wu-Tang: Shaolin Style, six years after the Clan’s first album.

The group whose concerts fill the new video was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on November 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Chris Rock introduced the group, with U-God among the members honored in the performer category. The ceremony brought the group together for a medley that included “C.R.E.A.M.” and a tribute to Ol’ Dirty Bastard through “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.”

The Clan’s next announced performance comes on Thanksgiving Day at Ford Field, when it headlines halftime of the Detroit Lions’ game against the Chicago Bears. Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith will sit in with the group, having previously played on a version of “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit” with RZA, Inspectah Deck and Method Man. CBS will broadcast the game at 1 p.m. Eastern on November 26.

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony airs on ABC on December 8, with the full ceremony streaming the next day on Disney+ and Hulu.
